episode.tagline: Complex AI. Explained visually. Built practically.
episode.title: API or MCP: How an AI Tutor Reaches the School's Lessons
episode.disclosure: Fictional teaching scenario based on researched conditions

onScreen.emphasis: Can an AI tutor follow the teacher's lessons, not the whole internet?

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Mrs Wanjiru teaches Kiswahili at a secondary school in Nairobi. Every evening she marks forty exercises by hand.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: She wants an AI tutor that follows her lessons, not the whole internet.

onScreen.title: API or MCP?
onScreen.subtitle: How an AI tutor reaches the school's lessons

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Welcome to the AI Workshop. Today: API, or MCP. What is the difference?

onScreen.caption: Listening to the teacher and her students

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Tanyi, I spoke with Mrs Wanjiru and her students. Here is what they said.

items.text: Follow my scheme of work, week by week
Never write the essay for a student
Mark practice exercises with my marking guide
We share the lab tablets, 2 or 3 to a screen
We want it to explain, not just give answers
We only use it on the school Wi-Fi

ui.title: Design rules
lines: 1. The teacher's notes are the only source
2. Shared devices: no names, no personal logins
3. Explain and mark. Never do the homework.

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Mrs Wanjiru was clear. Follow my scheme of work. Never write the essay for them. Mark with my guide.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: And the students?

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: They share lab tablets, two or three to a screen. And they want explanations, not answers.

left.title: API
items: Fixed requests, written by a developer
The program must know them in advance

right.title: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
items: One open standard for AI tools
Tools describe themselves in plain language
The AI reads, chooses, asks permission
Sits on top of the API

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: The notes live in the school's lesson folder. Software reaches it through an API: the service's own counter, with its own form. A developer fills the form in code, and the program repeats it exactly.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is an open standard for AI. The service describes its tools in plain language. The AI reads them, picks one, and asks permission. It does not replace the API. It sits on top.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: The tutor sees a short list of tools, and what each one is for.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: The MCP server holds those tools. It is the adapter.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Behind it, the same API into the lesson folder. Nothing magical.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: And the tutor only reads notes. Publishing to students stays with the teacher.

ui.title: rule.txt
lines: if question mentions a week → fetch notes

messages.text: Week 6 is noun classes. Source: Mrs Wanjiru's notes, week 6. Want a short explanation?

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Version one. The lesson folder API wants a subject and a week number. I write a connector.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Next, the exercise bank. A different API, with different rules. So, a second connector.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Now a rule. If the question mentions a week, fetch the notes. Otherwise, answer from memory.

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: What is in week six? It found the notes on noun classes. Nice.

lines.speaker: hallucinator
lines.text: A student asked what they learned about nouns yesterday. No week number, so no notes. So I answered. Beautifully. From a textbook that does not exist.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: The rule never fired. That is the difference. With a plain API, the developer decides when to call it, in code. The model cannot see it.

onScreen.title: Version 2: the same API, behind MCP

steps.title: Wrap the API in an MCP server

ui.title: tool: get_lesson_notes
lines: Returns Mrs Wanjiru's notes for a topic or week.
Use before answering any question about a lesson.
If nothing is found, say: ask your teacher.

ui.title: tool: mark_exercise
lines: Marks a student answer with the teacher's guide.
Never writes the essay. Hints only.

messages.text: What did we learn about nouns yesterday?
Checking Mrs Wanjiru's notes... Week 6, noun classes. Here is a short explanation and 1 practice question.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Version two. Same API, wrapped in an MCP server. The tool describes itself: what it returns, when to use it, and what to say when nothing is found.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Second tool: mark exercise. Teacher's guide only. Never writes the essay.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Same question, no week number. Now the model reads the description, sees it needs the notes, and calls the tool. MCP is not magic. It made the tool visible, and the rule enforceable.

messages.text: Write my essay about my school for tomorrow.
I can't write it for you. Here is an outline with 3 questions to answer in your own words.

ui.title: Tutor wants to publish 10 practice questions to class KISW-B

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Shared tablet, so no names. Enter the class code, and the session clears after forty minutes.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: One student tries it: write my essay. The tutor refuses, and hands back an outline.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: The tutor drafted ten practice questions. It cannot publish them. The teacher reads, then approves. Approved.

onScreen.title: Who owns this tutor?
items: Maintains: the school's ICT teacher runs the MCP server
Content: notes and marking guide stay Mrs Wanjiru's work
Data: sessions stay on the school's server, no names
Value: evenings back, and a question bank the school keeps
Accountable: the teacher approves everything students see

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: The notes and marking guide stay the teacher's work. Student sessions stay with the school, with no names attached.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: The school's ICT teacher maintains the MCP server. Mrs Wanjiru keeps the notes current, and approves everything students see. So she catches the tutor when it is wrong.

onScreen.emphasis: Pick one thing your AI needs to look up. Write 2 sentences: what the tool returns, and when to use it. That is an MCP tool description.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Your build challenge. Pick one thing your AI needs to look up. Write two sentences: what the tool returns, and when to use it. That is an MCP tool description.

lines.text: Don't just use AI. Build it to work reliably. See you in the next episode.

tanyi.name: Tanyi
tanyi.role: AI engineer and instructor, the animated host. Middle-aged Black African man. Calm, direct, practical. Has built and operated real systems.

amara.name: Amara
amara.role: Curious learner who asks the questions beginners are thinking.

kito.name: Kito
kito.role: Small AI assistant who demonstrates concepts and occasionally makes believable mistakes.

hallucinator.name: The Hallucinator
hallucinator.role: Mischievous. Represents confident but incorrect AI output.

gatekeeper.name: The Gatekeeper
gatekeeper.role: Represents security, privacy, governance and human approval.
